newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply up in active trading on Wednesday on heavy overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at 23,710 yuan ($2,858) per tonne, up 610 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 23,650 and hit a high of 23,820.
May rose 300 to 23,550, June 460 to 23,700, July 580 to 23,820 and September 610 to 23,770.
Combined volume rose sharply to 98,290 tonnes from 36,500.
Copper opened sharply higher and rose further with most contracts closing at or near their intra-day highs.
Traders said the LME gains boosted the confidence of Shanghai's long position holders with all the contracts breaching the 23,500 yuan resistance level.

"Large amounts of stop loss buying emerged with many investors believing the contracts will rise further in the next few days," one trader said. "The technical charts have improved a lot after today's sharp rises."
Physical average prices rose 100 yuan to 23,400 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area on Wednesday, thanks to the gains of the futures prices, traders said.
Traders said Shanghai copper futures would follow the trend on the LME in the next few days.
"Open interest fell sharply today indicating some investors are worried about the market trend to some extent," a second trader said.
"If LME copper can continue its strong upward trend, Shanghai copper futures will breach the key 24,000-yuan resistance level in the short term," he added.
Aluminium ended up, following copper's trend. May rose 290 to 15,450, June 350 to 15,750 and July 410 to 15,910.
Combined volume rose to 1,480 tonnes from 760. ($1=8.2945)
